reviews.text: 目前游戏没有任何挑战性，3个角色，输出角色带个1个主动技能都可以随便通关，全靠被动联动，大量2蓝以上的技能完全没有使用的必要，期待后续改进
要解锁角色一定要先通战役 战役从火山开始，难度有点高，怪都偏机制类的 需要特定卡牌应对，所以导致要重打几次，才能过的情况，游玩体验开始下降 万幸的是，火山过了以后，基本就是平推了，难度不大 肉鸽模式，流程略长，碰到某些机制怪，如果没有特定卡牌应对，基本就重开了 最终BOSS ，也卡的要死，需要优化一下 勉强给个好评 PS（减怪攻击卡，消负面卡必拿，多段攻击的卡也要有一张）
很好的游戏，但我现在的bug 是 无法读取之前的游戏数据，这样几乎导致我无法进入游戏。我宁愿重开一个账户接着玩，希望能快点解决

通关天启10了，太看运气了还没得SL商店药店只刷新一张卡BOSS宝箱直接没得选，还有过了天启9的彩蛋英雄出不出的？星爆的30级解锁的遗物有BUG，给自己人上buff的时候会把自己原本身上带的buff覆盖掉，给敌人上负面buff的时候也会把敌人原本身上带的负面buff覆盖掉，还有不知道是不是代码冲突了还是之前打的难度太简单没注意，天启10后所有每回合多少次的遗物都变成了每场战斗多少次，bug还是有点多不知道之后还会不会更新修复

《Dimensionals》是由Mino Games自研自发的一款美式卡通漫画风回合制肉鸽卡牌游戏，游戏里我们需要带领各次元宇宙的英雄组成3人小队去消灭次元裂缝领主。将不同的角色、不同的技能、不同的道具进行组合，用强大的阵容一路途径，最终拯救这个被侵略的宇宙。 游戏最值得肯定的是它的美术画风，标准的美式卡通漫画风，剧情过场全都以漫画的形式展示，各角色立绘也都有着相当可爱又不失威武的气势，游玩过程就像在看儿时最爱的卡通片似的！更为难得是游戏的剧情，标准的英雄拯救世界or宇宙的套路，这就太对味了！ 游戏的玩法其实相当简单，就是选择不同的英雄一路战斗，各英雄能配备不同的技能，技能以卡牌的形式展示，还分主动被动，搭配得好的情况下能让英雄的输出更上一个台阶，而且技能卡牌还能进阶。不过不同于常见的同类游戏那般一次能配备一堆卡组，在这里每个英雄最多携带3个卡，每次战斗之前可以调整，这虽然让战斗流派的构筑少了许多种可能，但却也激发我们去多尝试不同英雄的组合，也算是一个较为有想法的做法了。 整体而言，《Dimensionals》算是一款中规中矩的回合制肉鸽卡牌游戏，最大的亮点就是美术，玩法方面大差不差，而且更重要的是竟然没有中文！（我是真没想到一款介绍全中文的游戏竟然没中文的！！！）不过游戏目前还在EA阶段，流程也较短，可使用英雄也还较少，不知道以后更新版本会不会有什么大的变化，只能后面关注了！ [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]
正式版已经通关了第二季，比起第一季难度提高不少，需要运气耐心和技术。第3关超级难，多段打击闪避无效，SL了很多遍才过，需要火爪起手卖掉闪避的招换用熔妈的嘲讽在关键敌人大招时接住牺牲出局。第5关我是一次过没什么印象，大概就是小焰装了两个旋火一顿群攻秒3个小朋友。整体觉得是很有深度的游戏，比较对我的胃口很上头，那么多差评主要是机制没有易难度选项设置，也没设一个交流群，卡关就失去耐心了。
非常上瘾的一款肉鸽，卡牌？构筑的内容是角色的技能，感觉像是玩了一款买断制的回合制手游，但是游戏内容称得上是丰富，套路不一定有深度，但是可以玩的很爽。最值得好评的一点是，如果有的技能是随机取对象或造成随机伤害，玩家可以直观的看到这个技能即将打谁和打多少，随机技能再也不用去瞎猜结果是怎么样了，极大程度上帮助了伤害计算的精准性和可控性，这点特别好评
第二章章节3后面几波怪的难度设计有问题吧，玩家技能组也给得很弱。这关之前感觉不错，技能联动也很爽。
能不能给战役模式关卡加一次复活机会，我打到第四章了，经常因为第一次打不熟悉新英雄技能或者怪的机制出现失误，直接就崩盘了，那后面的战役一关有九到十个小关卡，需要打将近半个小时，重头再来一次太累了。或者你可以让我们开局自己选几个技能呀。现在这个战役容错低难度高还都是机制怪，对技能选取有要求，打的实在是累
还不错的游戏 角色不少 每一类角色流派都挺固定 剧情有点典 能玩个个把星期的

The game is really fun. The only thing that really annoys me is how slow the UI is, how unfriendly it is and how many clicks it needs EVERY TIME. There aren't even any shortcut keys so you actually have to click... EVERY TIME. The game itself is great. I love the theme and the gameplay as a whole is really fun. That being said... it does not seem like the company is doing very well, if it is still alive. That's sad. I would still recommend the game, though.

This is a tough game to review. It has a ton of neat ideas I haven't really seen explored much in this genre: * Hearthstone-style incrementing energy per turn * Really neat proc chaining (when you shield, passive A triggers, which triggers B, which triggers C, etc.) (similar to, say, Siralim) * The shopkeeper and potion seller are available between every combat * Being able to store excess potions in your inventory for later use is nice (instead of other games which would make you discard them) * Upgrading abilities with duplicates is well done * Previewing random effects & crits is unique Not to mention the beautiful art and characters. I love the style! And yet, it's got a lot of rough edges: * Way too many enemies do AOE or random targets on round 1, when you have only 1 energy, so can really only shield 1 character. It's effectively unavoidable damage early in a run and not fun. For the same reason, taunt feels pretty useless. * Near the end of the run, enemy damage scales so high it's unblockable without a dedicated block build, so I keep finding myself building for offense, which reduces replayability. * Passives & actives compete for slots, so: 1) "give a hero another slot" in an unreasonably high value upgrade (which makes its competing upgrades comparatively worthless). 2) because most passives can proc a lot, they're just plain more useful than actives, meaning often 2 characters do nothing but hold passives for the 3rd character to benefit from; 3) Combined with that, and the incrementing energy, and push for a glass cannon build, expensive actives are just plain unlikely to get used (when battles only last a round or two) * Lag: because everything is so heavily pushed towards procs triggering procs, 1) sometimes a single ability use can take 20 seconds to resolve; and 2) later in the game it can be impossible to track WHY something happened So in summary, it's worth checking out (but wait for a sale). I enjoyed my time with it, I just wish the devs had been able to do another balance and polish pass.

THIS GAME CAN BE PLAYED. The devs fixed the issue preventing people from starting the game and it 100% works now. With that being said, this is a really fun game that deserved more attention. The art is awesome. The characters are great. The gameplay is a lot of fun, and it's really fun trying different character combinations when going through the roguelike mode called Endless Raid. It has a really cool story that is, at times, very challenging and RNG-dependent, but fun overall. If you want to play a fun roguelike with interesting characters, this is still a really great game even if the devs aren't working on it anymore. The game is 100% complete and nothing is missing, so when you buy it you are getting the full 1.0 release with a ton of characters to unlock. It's a shame the game didn't get more attention so we got more characters added, but there's still a lot here to do and experience and I would give it a shot.

*Update: I'm changing my rating to a thumbs up because the game deserves it, but I'm leaving my original gripe below: Fun gameplay and character design, but I cannot stand clicking through hours of dialogue I don't really care about, in a game mode I don't want to play, just to unlock the characters I want to play in the rouge-like mode. After playing for 4 hours on release, I have not yet played a single minute of the actual game I want to play, and I still have multiple hours left before I unlock the new characters. Please, make the characters unlockable from completing challenges in the rouge-like mode instead of forcing me to click through 6+ hours of dialogue and story. I just want to play the game!

Genuinely a lot more content than I was expecting from an early access title. There is massive potential here with the art and the music and the combat! I think I can safely say this game is going to eat up a lot of my free time... Plus, Shork, I mean come on, a cat shark hybrid. I love him. Edit Update: The music is still stuck in my head. Weeks later. Still singing that damn theme.

I'm not a huge fan of turn-based games that play like a deck builder, but this was... surprisingly addicting? [h3] What I enjoyed about the game: [/h3] [*]A good handful of content for its launch and its price. The Campaign has around 8 episodes available for Season 1, which is set in the Water Dimension, with characters you can unlock. And even once you have completed that, you can do the Master Raid mode, which is like an endless mode for players who like to test the limits of their builds. [*] The game provides a summary of your Expedition run and a Timer in the settings, which is good for players who like to best their personal records. [*]Interesting enemy designs and writing. Even the earliest enemies show so much character, like the King Crab Specter, Ceviche. It has a shiny crown dangling from it's overgrown horn and even has interesting flavor dialogue such as "My golden Crown...how it sparkles in the resplendent ocean light.." and insults like "Ye of little culture!" made me laugh :)) I was not expecting to read that from a glorified crab. [*]Vibrant, animated environments and characters in comic style is just [i]chef's kiss[/i]. [*]Favourite characters are silly Shork and money grubbing Shopkeep ([spoiler]or should I say, "Regulus"[/spoiler]), together with their animations <3 Even without the voice acting, I can imagine what they sound like when I read the dialogue hahaha [h3] What I hope they can improve on while in the early access phase: [/h3] [*] I'm one of those players who is not a fan of reading tutorial windows and would rather skip it to get to the gameplay experience. Perhaps the devs can give the players the option to choose either "Skip Tutorial guide" (for players who want to learn on their own), or have a live overlay tutorial that a player can follow along and learn while playing at the same time, and it can pop in when the game presents something unfamiliar. And should the player want to read them again, they can be directed to the pause screen where they can access the tutorial guide, and show those detailed pop up windows that the current game is using. [*] Have Setting option to "Click to use" instead of dragging an ability to the target. I find clicking faster and more efficient. [*]Not knowing about the Resets. I wish there was a window pop up warning or an option to choose whether I keep or reset my build when I continue to the next episodes. I automatically assumed all my accumulated abilities would carry over once I click the next story, and am surprised when they don't appear and are instead replaced with new abilities. [*] Clarity of some Abilities. Perhaps the game could issue a warning or a sound that tells me when a move's requirements are not being met, because it feels like a waste of Mana when new players make small mistakes such as using Shork's 'Cover when he has no Defense to spend for the ability. [*]During Granny's potion shop in the tutorial, I was confused as to why my 41 remaining Gold could not buy a 40 Gold potion item. Strange. [*] Equippable and Non-Equippable Inventory. As a new player, there are times when I receive items that I'm not sure where they are used in. I think those are one of the moments I would appreciate a tutorial popping in. [*]Just a preference (and a bit of story spoiler), [spoiler]but wondering if I can see more "sad" or "concerned" emotions from Koa when he is referring to his missing Grandpa?[/spoiler] There is so much potential for improvement over the next updates and fixes, but I think Mino nailed it with the visuals and loveable charcters. Wishing them the best for this game! About Reviewing Player's usual preferences (for anyone's reference): immersion, story, stunning art, affordability, fast-paced, flavor dialogue, 2D, 1st person shooters, 3rd person RPGs, Side scroller, metroidvanias, lore

Love the game and not only that, the team behind it has been amazing with the community, quickly fixing any issue: •After I and a few other players faced a bug, they were quick to respond and in less than a day they sent us a Key to a beta version with the bug fixed, as they prepare the new hotfix. Special big thanks to Rodrigo on that. Regarding my opinion on the game: •The game is great, I love roguelikes, and this one has the vibes of old cartoons I used to watch, and mix it quite nicely. •visual and music are nice •the gameplay is nice, I like the fact there are ‘premade’ teams that you can mix and match •Comparing it to other roguelikes, I’ll say there are still a couple of things where this game could improve: 1)for someone who has played lots of roguelikes, the game isn’t particularly difficult. I don’t think it’s an issue at base level, but maybe some higher difficulty modes would be appreciated (if I’m not wrong though, they are already working on it) 2)The element of having to unlock characters through story mode may not be for everyone, I feel like it should be optional probably. Personally I like playing the story, it offers lots of funny dialogues, but I understand it’s not everyone’s jam. A skip button on the dialogue could also work. Regardless of these 2 minor issues (which I have no doubt will be fixed) the game is amazing, I love it and I know it has still a lot of potential even

First impression is pretty good! The roguelike mode seems to be the main catch of the game, it's pretty in-depth, and it's got a lot of different upgrades you can choose, and also a lot of characters. I also tried out the first chapter of story mode, it's not bad but I do wish it was a little less linear, compared to the roguelike mode it's a lot more simple. Game is still in early access though, so hopefully they can add more to it down the line, but even then I recommend it for the price 👍

Dimensionals is a simple and accessible game for those who enjoy defeating villains by casually dragging the mouse while holding a cup of coffee in the other hand. Graphics and Design The visuals are cute and well-crafted, with a style reminiscent of games like Griftlands. Shork is adorable. The protagonist sticks to a (purposely?) generic design. Gameplay Simple and accessible, making it ideal for beginners or anyone looking for a more casual experience. The drag-and-drop mechanics for abilities are a little slow but functional, making the game fully playable with just a mouse — great for accessibility. The combat is straightforward yet effective, good for newcomers to turn-based tactics or players seeking a relaxed experience. It still lacks the depth of veteran titles, but it’s just launched in Early Access. Challenge and Difficulty The game’s early hours offer low-challenge combat, perfect for new players but possibly too simple for those looking for depth. Technical Aspects No bugs were encountered during the first few hours. Overall, it’s a solid game, especially for an early access title. It has plenty of potential for growth. Rating: 3,5 Shorks out of 5.
我更改评论是因为我过了，但是剧情关卡难易度要优先调整，必须优先调整！因为我不想在一个熟悉角色的关卡里打的那么累，再次点名火焰关卡第5关的3个史莱姆，在你们没有解决问题之前我不会给予好评！
出现读取存档的错误进不去的话，点击设置，在设置页面最下面有一个清除当前挑战按钮。能救一个是一个。
火焰第3关打了7，8边过不去，一个垃圾坦，一个完全没用的辅助闪避，一个伤害垃圾的主角。怪动不动就5下20，一下80，打它叠伤害，不打他也叠伤害，真有几个人过了这关吗？游戏开发者自己玩过吗？技能随机性这么强，光靠给的几百金剧情里压根没办法选到合适的技能，一个剧情关第2章打了重复一关打了6个多小时，差评
欠缺打磨，太可惜了架构那么好，官方也不打算打磨下去了
剧情模式还没玩那个啥火5，但肉鸽最终BOSS。。。 先是突出一个卡，它机制多到整个游戏每动一次都开始卡了。 20个机制？我是懒得看了。 打它之前其他哪些BOSS，我无伤过。它嘛，我没想能过。 其他各种小BUG多得啊。 就那种升级卡牌没效果这么明显的BUG都能有。
解锁蜘蛛侠任务怎么完成啊，影袭的利刃王牌使用52次，还是一次攻击造成52次伤害啊，使用了都不止100次了，怎么解锁啊
说真的，作为一个只对rogue游戏的感兴趣的玩家不能理解官方为什么强迫玩家必须玩战役模式，当然第二章以前我尚能接受，就当看个播片，但到第二章难度直线上升，失败都是因为没刷到优良的技能，战役模式的难度明显不合理，制作人可能受ben10这种动画影响，有这种外星英雄情怀，但作为并无这种情怀的玩家，我实在不想在战役模式受折磨。
数值问题严重，懒得说了 玩了12小时，还没通关，怀疑人生。过场动画磨磨唧唧，还有就是怪物数值在第二关后涨的很厉害，没拿好东西就基本没了。遗物系统很鸡肋。拿了和没拿没多少区别。受不了了。最近应该不会想玩了。 手贱又玩了，最后一关boss,我电脑呼呼的吹，还有些卡
我以为火5的反甲史莱姆已经是极限对抗了，火7是真的变态，兄弟，你要不要自己开一把，看看能不能打赢？

其他玩法都不错，但是火焰第五关有能打过去的吗？试过无数次了，没有任何回血机制，前面几波小怪不断磨血，3个史奈姆怎么打都暴毙，500血反伤，3个英雄加一块都没他反伤多，而且另外2个史奈姆一个提高敌人增伤，一个提高我方易伤 任务选择的3个英雄，既不能叠加伤害，又没有防御护盾，唯一自身增伤的还只能叠10层，都得靠多段攻击打伤害，正中史奈姆下怀，目测史奈姆后面还有一个boss战吧，即便能过，到boss血都磨没了，史奈姆从前面4波小怪打死后，最多也就8次左右的抽卡或买卡改命的机会，明牌全自选估计都没有能打过去的组合吧？

Really good effort from the devs for branching out!! Had fun, and I got my money's worth, but it pains me that I can't recommend without some asterisks. Plays like a $10-$15 mobile game. Needs a LOT more polish (performance, sound, some UI stuff, etc.). Character design and worldbuilding are good. Gameplay is standard. Performance, sound design, UI, and everything else needs help. It's clear this comes from a game studio that is more familiar with making mobile games. If this was sold on mobile for $7, it'd be an easy recommend. But on pc which has a higher standard for games for $20? Unfortunately not. Rough edges: the shop button is always present, but only clickable when outside of any other contextual menus. buying a discounted item from the shop doesn't discount how much you can sell it for some sounds, like the victory sound, sound cheap why do characters attacks jump below the screen when an enemy is attacking? I'm sure there's more... If you know you're going to like playing a game like this, go for it. If you're unsure, something like Slay the Spire and Inscryption are much higher recommends.

2 issues: 1. The game is very unbalanced. Most fights are so easy you steamroll through the enemies. Then you encounter an enemy that is wildly overtuned that is impossible to beat. 2. The content takes too long to unlock. I just want to play the roguelike mode with some new characters. It takes 30 min going through unskippable dialogue in the campaign to unlock 1 new character. This game has a lot of potential if some issues can be fixed

As of Dec 3rd, 2025 this is a painstakingly discovered workaround that should allow anyone who has a copy of Dimensionals to operated it, despite the missing responses from devs and Steam's inability to help. My process is detailed here, along with my suppositions of what made Dimensionals work. This is by no means a sales pitch to pay full price for a game that is unsupported, but it is a workaround for anyone who does want to enjoy the game in its current state. With that aside... here we go, and good luck! 1) My first step was to disable my internet connectivity, restarted steam in offline mode, then started Dimensionals. -- This step might work if you simply disable the internet connection, see below. 2) Once the game boots up the "Play" button should turn yellow/gold. Click "Play" then accept the conditions about cloud saves that asks you to press yes 5 times, and do so. 3) Once in the game, I had to play the tutorial (my first time playing it was after the game no longer being available). I believe that you have to play a level of the campaign, or something else that forces the save to occur. I've been unable to wipe the save and try again to test further (I restarted the game after finishing the tutorial, and it made me repeat the tutorial when I launched it again). -- Note: When I finished the tutorial the second time I played 2 scenarios in the campaign, played the roguelite mode, the game crashed (due to a bug), and when I restarted the game (still offline) it restarted me from that point in the battle. 4) After that I could close down the game, and Dimensionals would load and maintain my progress. Once the game has gotten past the main menu, internet connectivity can be restored without affecting gameplay (to my testing so far). -- Caveat: To be able to press "Play" to get past the steam authentication, internet connectivity has to be disabled, the conditions agreee, 5x Yes... and then the game would function normally, even if I restore internet connectivity while the game is operational. Hopefully this makes the game available to those who like it, want to play it, or are stuck with a purchase they made due to the lack of response from the dev team or steam. Feel free to send me a message and let me know if this worked for you! It would warm m heart to know that my efforts managed to help anyone else! It is my sincere hope that anyone reading this has a wonderful gaming experience whether Dimensionals or something else!! All the best of gaming to you!!!!

The game appears to have been abandoned by the developers. Tried to boot and like many other users the game cannot access save data. According to the official Discord it appears that the development team may have been dissolved and nobody has heard anything recently about further support. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.

Content bare, poor balance, focused on nerfs only to heroes, which are still broken, while the same one boss has been poorly designed since its creation, if you were looking for a decent quality roguelike card game, look elsewhere.

The balance as it stands right now is way off. If you don't make a perfect build, you're screwed. The bosses ramp so much faster than the other battles that they tend to just blow you out of the water and nothing you could do can salvage it. I hope to come back and like this game after some balance adjustments, because the core idea and presentation and stuff is phenomenal. I just can't recommend it with the current difficulty.

Great art and story style! Game play has a lot of potential but it really needs some balancing. Some fights are so easy they only serve as a task you have to do to get an upgrade. Then on the other hand some fights are so hard that they feel unwinnable. It also doesn't feel like there is a lot of variety in the builds per character. Seem like victory comes from corruption stacking or damage buff stacking and not much else. I'm not unhappy I bought the game and I'm hoping that when I try it after early access, it will be much improved. However in the current state I wouldn't recommend it unless you want to support the development because it really does have a lot of promise if they can balance it. Will update later.

Man, I really enjoyed this game earlier this year. Took a break to play other things, came back, and suddenly it's unplayable (see other recent reviews about server connectivity). Really disappointing.

The devs went MIA after the last update on this and you can't play this unless you do some workaround to get it to boot after the title screen. Don't bother with this one, its a bricked and abandoned game. Like other recent reviews as of this time say its a Smash and Grab by the now dissolved dev team.

I do like turn based roguelikes, and I totally didn't buy it because I'm huffing copium hoping they make another Mino Monsters game. Fun, but seeing the character I really wanted to use both not in the game AND will be locked behind story progression in the future made me sort of sad. [i] “Baby shark, doo, doo, doo, doo, doo, doo” ~ Shork (the chonky cat shark hybrid), 2024. I suffered, so you should too. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + Comic book inspired UX + Focused and consistent art direction + Playful, and at times, comical writing + Characters have charming designs and are filled with personality + Skills are well thought out, offering various playstyles and several ways to progress + The procedurally generated Roguelike adventure modes offer a decent amount of replayability 🟥 Cons: - Merging skills costs gold - Lacks traditional meta progression - The campaign is relatively easy and linear - Needs more music variety (especially considering the quality of everything else) - When starting a new run, some skills being in your inventory rather than being equipped (why?) 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Option to replace drag and drop with click to use ~ Remove (or reduce) gold costs for merging & tiering up skills ~ Update the name of Relics to show ‘Relic’ rather than ‘Skill’ when acquired [h1] There's Nothing Bad to Say [/h1] Dimensionals is a roguelike deck builder, similar to Slay the Spire and the likes. Featuring a colourful cast of characters, comical writing, and an engaging loop, it’s sure to please fans of the genre. If you’re looking for deep and lengthy meta progression however, this one may not be for you. You’ve three characters, each having up to four (active and passive) skill slots. Each turn you gain one point of mana (more via certain skills), increasing by one every turn (up to a maximum of 10). You can use any number of skills from any number of characters, should their costs and cooldowns allow. There are plenty of (upgradable) skills (offensive, defensive, supporting) of various rarities and tiers to play around with, offering a variety of ways to progress. Additionally, you’ve a backpack for items which, just like skills, will either enhance your party or hinder your enemies. Finally, there are relics, which can make or break your run (depending on if they’re positive or negative). Whether you like or dislike Dimensionals will depend on how much you like traditional meta progression. Here, you need to play through the unnecessarily easy story to unlock additional characters, who will come with their own newly unlocked skills (cards). While I do enjoy it and it offers massive amounts of content and replay value, your mileage may vary. This game is fun and does a lot of things well. The character designs are top notch, and there's lots of room for interesting builds, and the core loop is not tedious. There are two modes: a rougelite mode where you can level up your heroes over the course of your adventures, and a story mode that takes you through some pre-determined fights and light character arcs. The story mode is really designed to showcase and introduce new skills/characters while the rougelite mode is a lot more of what you'd expect from a game like this. I really like this game and want to give it a thumbs up, but right now I cannot. The current version can soft lock you out of doing anything at the end of your turn (mostly seen in boss fights from my experience). Closing and reopening the game temporarily fixes the issue, but only for one turn. You can brute force your way through a boss fight by restarting the game about a dozen times, but it grinds everything that's good about the game to a screeching halt. I am sure that this will get patched out soon and I am happy to change my review to a thumbs up once this bug is addressed, but right now the game feels unplayable. __________ Edit: Looks like the softlock bug is fixed!

So my thoughts after playing for about 8 hrs including the demo. The skill cards need a complete rework plain and simple, because 90% of them are nearly useless. As an example the skill does 20 damage with no multi hit a crit chance boost which when it crits it doubles the damage so that's fine but the boss has 15k health and in 10-15 turns it will one shot you, also being restricted to 9 of these 12 if you maxed the hero slots. Most of these slots are sucked up by skills to give your characters rage and curse the bosses just so you can kill them in time. So in reality you end up with 3-6 slots for skills because all of the others are passives just so you can stack some buffs/debuffs. The game in its current state is literally me just trying to force a few different builds that actually work by refreshing the shop every chance i get in the hopes that i don't get all trash. Now i understand making a deck builder is very hard, but in the current state i say the game is not worth PAYING FOR that is the key here. Sorry guys, but I don't really know what you were thinking with this one. I've played dozens of deckbuilder roguelikes - the genre is saturated, so if you're going to wade into this market you need to bring your A game, and unfortunately Dimensionals is a C game at best, unplayable at worst. The game's content is gated behind a frankly obnoxious series of "volumes" like a comic book series - a set of story missions you have to progress through to unlock new characters etc. I am on like book 5 of the Fire Dimension series in which you pick up Inferna and learn how to use her abilities. In this particular story, you are given no defensive tools whatsoever other than ones you randomly acquire and your robot's awful random defense allocation passive (this game loves random btw). The enemies all do massive AOE attacks that get more powerful every time you hit them, and given that you have no defensive tools, you get hit all the time, no way to mitigate, no way to heal. I have attempted this stupid book THREE TIMES, each time frantically clicking through the cute but quickly interminable and unskippable dialogue sequences that accompany every.....single.....fight.......and every time I come up against the blob that deals 10 damage every time it gets hits (did I mention all your abilities deal random damage to random enemeies all the time? This procs that 10 damage every time). The fact that this game's silly cartoon dialogue is unskippable is frankly an insult - I'm not playing Baldur's Gate 3, I'm playing a silly little roguelike with surface-level mechanics. At the stage of the game I'm at (and as you can see I've played for a full twelve hours) there is only one build - generating more and more rage and/or corruption to overwhelm your enemies, that's it. I don't need to see generic white kid flirt with a sexualised elemental avatar fifteen times when I just want to get out of the scripted story mode with its scripted abilities and characters you have to start with and get to YOUR ACTUAL GAME. I've played Astrea: Six Sided Oracles and won with every character on multiple difficulties - this is not a skill issue. Me winning the book I'm stuck on is entirely in the lap of the gods, and I just can't. I'm done. Bad game, obsessed with its own whimsical, Saturday morning cartoon theme, music is repetitive and uninspired, art direction is fine, concept is fine but stale (Dimensions based on the four elements? Originality overload) and commits the ultimate sin - stops me playing, simply because I cannot play it. Guys, sort out your story campaign - make it as easy as you can, and leave all the hardcore nonsense for endgame ONLY.
